title: A Robot Hand Like Thing Can Walk, Type and Play a Game
summary:
Halloween is almost here, and engineers have built a robot that looks like Thing, the creepy hand from The Addams Family. It is a robot hand with no arm or body. It can balance on its own fingertips and creep along the ground.

A team at the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich in Switzerland built it. They started with a robot hand that has five fingers and 20 moving joints. Then they added a battery, motion sensors and a tiny computer on the back. With those extras, the whole thing weighs 1.8 pounds.

Teaching the hand to balance was tricky, because human hands have fingers of different lengths. The team trained the software in a computer simulation using reinforcement learning, which gives the software a reward each time it does something right.

Then the team tested the hand in 14 different places, indoors and outdoors. It crept across carpet, gravel, grass and metal with a springy, spider-like walk. It could also push a small cube while balancing on its other fingers. It even typed on a keyboard, hitting the right key 29 out of 32 times. And it played a puzzle video game called Sokoban by pressing the arrow keys in the right order.

The team says the idea could be useful later. A humanoid robot working in a tight space might send its detached hand to fetch something it cannot reach. The researchers wrote that giving robotic hands their own mobility could make future robots more versatile. The work is a preprint, which means other scientists have not yet reviewed it.
why_it_matters: Robots that can reach into tight spaces or handle tools made for people could be more helpful in the future.
